title: Local complete intersections over a field have Cohen-Macaulay stalks
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field] and $X$ a scheme locally of finite type over $k$ [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Suppose $X$ has an affine open cover whose coordinate rings are local complete intersections over $k$ [def-weil-pbc-complete-intersection-over-field]. Then every local ring $\mathcal O_{X,x}$ is Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] and Cohen-Macaulay: $\operatorname{depth}(\mathcal O_{X,x})=\dim\mathcal O_{X,x}$ [def-weil-pbc-depth, def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring]. Here $x$ ranges over all points of $X$, not only closed points.

source.place: Tag 00SB, lemma-lci-CM, applied on affine charts; Cohen-Macaulay ring means that every prime localization is Cohen-Macaulay.

proof.text: Fix an arbitrary point $x\in X$. Choose an affine chart $U=\operatorname{Spec}S$ of the hypothesized cover containing $x$. The affine-open stalk lemma identifies $\mathcal O_{X,x}$ with $S_{\mathfrak p}$ for the prime $\mathfrak p$ corresponding to $x$. By the definition of local complete intersection there is $g\notin\mathfrak p$ among the covering elements such that $T=S_g$ is a global complete intersection. No closedness assumption on $x$ has been made.

source.place: Tag 00SB, lemma-lci-CM, first reduction to a global complete intersection; Schemes Tag 01HV, lemma-spec-sheaves (6), for the affine stalk

proof.text:
Set $\mathfrak q=\{s/g^a:s\in\mathfrak p\}\subset T$. The fraction relation and $g
otin\mathfrak p$ show membership is independent of representatives; the ideal and primality conditions follow from those of $\mathfrak p$. There are inverse ring maps $S_{\mathfrak p}	o T_{\mathfrak q}$, $s/t\mapsto(s/1)/(t/1)$, and $T_{\mathfrak q}	o S_{\mathfrak p}$, $(s/g^a)/(t/g^b)\mapsto(sg^b)/(g^at)$. Here $t
otin\mathfrak p$ makes the latter denominator admissible. The fraction relations verify well-definedness, and substitution gives both composites equal to the identity. In particular $\mathcal O_{X,x}\cong T_{\mathfrak q}$, and $T
eq0$ because it has the prime $\mathfrak q$.

source.place: Tag 00CO, definition-localization, fraction relations; the local reduction at the beginning of Tag 00SB

proof.text: Choose the presentation $T\cong P/J$, where $P=k[y_1,\ldots,y_n]$, $J=(f_1,\ldots,f_c)$, and $\dim T=n-c$, supplied by the global-complete-intersection definition. Regard $\mathfrak q$ as a prime of $P/J$, and let $\mathfrak r$ be its inverse image in $P$. Thus $J\subseteq\mathfrak r$. Put $R=P_{\mathfrak r}$ and $a_j=f_j/1$. The polynomial-ring regularity node gives that $R$ is a Noetherian regular local ring. The global-complete-intersection regular-sequence node applies because $T\neq0$ and $\dim T=n-c$; it gives that $a_1,\ldots,a_c$ is an $R$-regular sequence. The localization-of-quotient node identifies $T_{\mathfrak q}$ with $R/JR=R/(a_1,\ldots,a_c)$, by the map taking a class of a fraction to the corresponding fraction of classes.

source.place: Tags 00SB, lemma-lci-CM, and 00SC, lemma-lci, proof (regular sequence at an arbitrary prime); Tag 00OQ, proposition-finite-gl-dim-polynomial-ring; Tag 00CT, proposition-localize-quotient

proof.text: Write $d=\dim R$. Since $R$ is regular local, its maximal ideal has a generating list $z_1,\ldots,z_d$. The regular-local-generators node says this list is $R$-regular. It lies in the maximal ideal, so the depth definition gives $\operatorname{depth}(R)\ge d$. This establishes the Cohen--Macaulay lower bound needed for the base case of the next induction, without making any assertion that the prime $\mathfrak r$ is maximal in $P$.

source.place: Tag 00NQ, lemma-regular-ring-CM, as used in Tag 00SB; Tag 00LI, definition-depth

proof.text: For $0\le i\le c$ put $R_i=R/(a_1,\ldots,a_i)$. Induct on $i$ with invariant: $R_i$ is a nonzero Noetherian local ring and $\operatorname{depth}(R_i)\ge\dim R_i$. At $i=0$ use $R_0=R$ and step 4. If $i<c$, regularity of the defining sequence says that multiplication by the class $\bar a_{i+1}$ is injective on $R_i$. Since $a_{i+1}\in\mathfrak rR$, this class lies in the maximal ideal of $R_i$; the local-quotient structure node identifies that ideal as the image of $\mathfrak rR$. Apply the Cohen--Macaulay nonzerodivisor-quotient node to $(R_i,\bar a_{i+1})$. It gives a nonzero Noetherian local quotient of dimension $\dim R_i-1$ with depth at least that dimension. This quotient is $R_{i+1}$: the maps in both directions send the iterated class of $r$ to the class of $r$ modulo $(a_1,\ldots,a_{i+1})$, and their kernels are exactly that ideal. This proves the inductive step. In particular $B=R_c$ is Noetherian local and $\operatorname{depth}(B)\ge\dim B$.

source.place: Tag 02JN, lemma-reformulate-CM, successive quotients by a regular sequence, with its one-element case iterated; Tag 00LF, definition-regular-sequence

proof.text: Apply the depth bound to the nonzero finite $B$-module $M=B$ (generated by $1$). Its support is all of $\operatorname{Spec}B$: for every prime $\mathfrak b$, the localization $B_{\mathfrak b}$ is nonzero, since $1/1=0$ would imply $s=0$ for some $s\notin\mathfrak b$. Hence the definition of support dimension in that bound is precisely the prime-chain definition of $\dim B$. We get $\operatorname{depth}(B)\le\dim B$, and step 5 gives equality. The isomorphisms from steps 1--3 identify $\mathcal O_{X,x}$ with $B$. A ring isomorphism bijects ideals and prime chains, takes the unique maximal ideal to the unique maximal ideal, and identifies multiplication on every successive quotient; therefore it preserves Noetherianity, Krull dimension, and the lengths of regular sequences defining depth. Thus $\mathcal O_{X,x}$ is Noetherian and has depth equal to dimension. Since $x$ was arbitrary this proves the assertion at every point.
